title: Cancel daemon startup readiness waits before forced stop escalation

criteria: A real owned leaf that accepts connections without answering HTTP is interrupted by shutdown before the original ten-second readiness deadline; the child is terminated and no service record survives.
Cancellation never signals or adopts an unrelated listener and prevents further boot service spawns while preserving earlier owned children for teardown.
The daemon enters common teardown when boot was cancelled and wakes from its supervision wait without changing the supervision cadence or stop escalation deadlines.
Existing readiness, process ownership, stop deadline and port-release regressions remain intact; no new dependency or unsafe allowance is introduced.
A and B require separate complete integration and production qualification; measured Linux installed start/health/stop and rollback evidence remains required before promotion.

notes: Scoped B only. Root will qualify the gate-repaired A before integrating this change. Windows native stop still uses its existing forced process-tree termination; Linux measurements do not claim graceful Windows shutdown.

validation.qualification: Development tests only. Root must integrate against the separately qualified gate-repaired A and qualify production B; installed performance and A-to-B-to-A rollback are pending.
validation.existing_optional_leaf_test: May return early without standalone service binaries; the new regression compiles and executes its own real Rust leaf and does not rely on that optional test.
